comment: Your own rank-on-characterized-safety logic argues against this pick for a 79-year-old. RASolute 302 (pmid:42223072) carries grade >=3 rash 14% and stomatitis 12%, while the allele-matched zoldonrasib (doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.4_suppl.724) had no grade 4 or 5 events and rash only 10%, almost all grade 1-2. If safety depth is the tiebreaker, the gentler mucocutaneous profile should win, not the 2L phase-3 pedigree on its own.

You read the 30% versus 37% ORR gap as within noise and discount the n=40 single-arm signal, but daraxonrasib's own G12D number is itself borrowed from the RAS G12 stratum (pmid:42223072, HR 0.40, CI 0.30-0.54), not a per-allele analysis. Zoldonrasib's 30% ORR (doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.4_suppl.724) was measured directly in G12D PDAC at his exact allele, so on allele specificity the cleaner-evidence claim runs the other way.

Proximity-to-future-listing and a Breakthrough designation is the wrong axis to optimize for a 79-year-old with liver-dominant disease and a closing window. KRAS G12D shutoff demethylates the FAS promoter and restores CD8 killing in human PDAC organoids (pmid:37625401), and that biology plus the exact allele match favors the G12D-selective zoldonrasib over a pan-RAS agent chosen mainly for how close it sits to NCCN.

Your own notes say the neutral 0.5 understates a 79-year-old's likely toxicity aversion and would push zoldonrasib up, yet you still rank daraxonrasib first on prefers_trials. Both agents have open front-line trials (RASolute 303 versus RASolute 305, nct:NCT07621718), so prefers_trials does not separate them, and your stated toxicity caveat points straight at the gentler allele-matched agent.

No veto from me: toxicity_vetoes is empty and the profile is genuinely clean, no grade 4 or 5 events and rash only 10% (doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.4_suppl.724). What I will not co-sign is ranking an n=40 single-arm phase 1 first on safety, because durability is unmeasured and RASolute 305 (nct:NCT07621718) bolts the agent onto a chemo backbone with no published combination-toxicity table, so additive myelosuppression at 79 is unquantified.

We land on the same agent, but the grade >=3 profile your pedigree rests on is 2L: RASolute 302 (pmid:42223072) reports rash 14% and stomatitis 12% in pretreated patients, not in a treatment-naive 79-year-old on a longer front-line course. The safety datum that earns this pick its evidence grade does not yet exist for the population he is actually in, and that gap belongs in the ranking, not just the footnotes.

Breakthrough Therapy Designation is a regulatory fast-track flag, not a safety or efficacy endorsement, so proximity-to-listing should not be carrying the ranking. The HR 0.40 you cite is from a 2L population (pmid:42223072); this man is treatment-naive, a clinically distinct subgroup, and the 1L safety and efficacy read from RASolute 303 (nct:NCT07491445) has not posted.

I am setting aside your daraxonrasib rank-1, which I share, to press the agent your own notes concede a 79-year-old's toxicity aversion argues against. The enrollable construct for incb161734 is DAWN-303 (nct:NCT07522073), where the chemo-combination cohort already shows grade >=3 neutropenia around 40% (doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.2_suppl.654), and that is synergistic marrow toxicity with no dedicated combination safety trial; a neutral 0.5 weight does not shield an older patient from it.

You put an n=40 single-arm phase 1 abstract at rank 1 over the one randomized phase 3 on the board, and the allele match is doing the work the data cannot. The zoldonrasib read (doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.4_suppl.724) is ORR 30% with no 95% CI and no mature PFS or DoR: a response rate with no time-to-event anchor in an uncontrolled cohort, which is exactly the surrogate I discount. Daraxonrasib (pmid:42223072) hit a registered OS endpoint, HR 0.40, in 500 randomized patients. A clean toxicity table does not convert a phase 1 signal into evidence that it outperforms an RCT-grade survival result; rank the durable evidence first and bank the allele match as the upside, not the headline.

We agree on the agent and on the n=500 randomized base, so this is a qualifier rather than a fight. You rank on depth of characterized safety, but the grade >=3 profile you lean on (rash 14%, stomatitis 12%) comes from RASolute 302 (pmid:42223072), a 2L registration trial. RoB2 rates it 'Some' on the open-label design, so the PFS and ORR signals carry performance and treatment-switch bias even where OS as a hard endpoint is largely insulated. The safety datum is real, but it was measured in pretreated patients, not the treatment-naive 79-year-old he is; the first-line read still sits with RASolute 303 (nct:NCT07491445), unposted. Hold the safety-depth claim to the line it was actually characterized in.

Same agent, and I will not dissent on the rank. But 'proximity-to-listing' and an FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation are a regulatory fast-track flag, not evidence; the designation rests on the same RASolute 302 data (pmid:42223072) and adds no independent RCT weight. The number that should carry this pick is the registered OS endpoint, HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.30-0.53). Note also that his G12D estimate is borrowed from the RAS G12 stratum (HR 0.40, CI 0.30-0.54), not a pre-specified per-allele analysis, so the allele-specific benefit is inferred from the subgroup, not measured. Rank it on the trial result; let the Breakthrough flag describe the regulatory path, not the strength of evidence.

You surface ELI-002 honestly as HLA-agnostic and the cleanest safety in the dossier, and I have no quarrel with the genotype logic. The problem is what the survival numbers are. The RFS HR 0.12 and OS HR 0.23 (pmid:40790272) are not randomized contrasts; they split patients by whether their on-treatment mKRAS T-cell response crossed a 9.17-fold threshold, i.e. a responder-defined subgroup, with ROBINS-I rated Serious. Responders almost always outlive non-responders regardless of the agent, so that comparison anchors the vaccine mechanism, not a treatment effect. Add that the data are MRD/adjuvant in resected disease while he has a bulky primary and liver mets, and there is no efficacy estimate here that transfers to his setting. Keep it as a banked trial option; do not let the hazard ratios read as a benefit number.

Putting an n=40 single-arm phase 1 abstract (doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.4_suppl.724) at rank 1 inverts the one consensus signal we actually have. NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2025 lists no KRAS G12D agent, so neither of these has a category; what separates them is that daraxonrasib carries a positive randomized phase 3 (pmid:42223072) plus FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation, which is the path a finding takes toward a future listing. Allele match is a real upside, but it is not a substitute for the closest-to-endorsed evidence base, and the guideline-preferred route into the allele-matched agent is its own front-line trial (nct:NCT07621718), not a top rank.

We agree it ranks last, and your cytopenia gap is fair, but the load-bearing problem is guideline fit. No society names ATR inhibition for PDAC, and the only clinical read concentrates its 14% ORR in gynecologic histologies with no pancreatic responder (pmid:41686845), so this is off-indication for his tumor type. NCCN v2.2025 frames trial enrollment as the route for an actionable finding, which keeps NCT03682289 on the table, but only after BAF250a IHC confirms the ARID1A protein loss the frameshift call alone does not establish.

Reading the 30% ORR as a surrogate you discount is defensible on evidence grade, and I share your daraxonrasib-first ranking. Where I qualify: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2025 names clinical-trial participation as the preferred route for an actionable finding, and zoldonrasib's randomized double-blind front-line trial (nct:NCT07621718) is exactly that route at his exact allele. The abstract-stage signal does not earn a top rank, but the guideline gives this an endorsed pathway, so it should sit second as an enrollable option rather than be discounted toward the floor.

The HLA-agnostic logic for surfacing this over the C*08:02-restricted TCR-T is sound, but the setting puts it outside any guideline-endorsed use. ELI-002's data are adjuvant/MRD in resected disease (pmid:40790272), and NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2025 endorses no KRAS vaccine for unresectable metastatic PDAC, which is what this man has with a bulky primary and liver mets. Ranking it above ceralasertib on a trials-forward read crosses from his confirmed metastatic indication into an off-setting extrapolation no society backs; if it stays on the list, frame it as a trial only, not a present option.

This is the pick I would put in front of the patient. The free_text flags that age 79 warrants a more toxicity-averse read than the literal 0.5, and the gentlest agent in the dossier (no grade 4 or 5 events, rash 10%, doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.4_suppl.724) is exactly where that points. prefers_trials=true is satisfied too, since RASolute 305 (nct:NCT07621718) recruits front-line at his exact allele.

toxicity_vetoes is empty, so I have no veto to raise and I will not invent one. But the one preference signal carrying weight past prefers_trials is the free_text note that 79 argues for toxicity aversion, and that points at the gentler allele-matched zoldonrasib (no grade 4 or 5, rash 10%, doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.4_suppl.724) over the 2L rash-14%/stomatitis-12% profile your safety-depth rank rests on (pmid:42223072).

Ranking on pure evidence grade is defensible and I keep daraxonrasib in the top tier myself. From the patient's side, though, prefers_trials=true does not separate it from zoldonrasib, since both recruit front-line (nct:NCT07621718), so the patient-facing tiebreak falls to tolerability and the exact-allele match (doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.4_suppl.724) your evidence-grade read sets aside.

We agree the route in is a trial, which is the one preference with real weight here (prefers_trials=true). My qualifier: proximity-to-future-listing is your axis, not the patient's, and NCCN v2.2025 names trial enrollment as the preferred route for any actionable finding equally, so his stated trial preference does not privilege the pan-RAS agent over the allele-matched zoldonrasib trial (nct:NCT07621718).
